chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ishaq ibn Ghalib who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gathers the first ones and the last ones, behold, they will see a person approaching, whose form has never been seen to be more handsome. When the believers look at him, and he is the Qur'an, they will say: 'This is from us, this is the most beautiful thing we have seen.' When he reaches them, he passes them. Then the martyrs look at him, and when he reaches the last of them, he passes them, and they say: 'This is the Qur'an,' and he passes them all. Until he reaches the Messengers, and they say: 'This is the Qur'an,' and he passes them until he reaches the Angels, and they say: 'This is the Qur'an,' and he passes them, until he comes to stand on the right side of the Throne. Then the Almighty will say: 'By My Might and Majesty, and the loftiness of My position, I will honour today the one who honoured you, and humble the one who humiliated you.'

key_terms.الْأَوَّلِينَ وَالْآخِرِينَ: The first and the last (all of creation)
key_terms.الْقُرْآنُ: The Qur'an, personified here as a handsome figure

ai.seo_question: How does the Qur'an appear on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this renowned hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes the personification of the Qur'an as a radiant figure who is recognized and granted passage by believers, martyrs, prophets, and angels on the Day of Judgment. This narrative underscores the ontological status of the Qur'an as a distinct entity and highlights the principle of *tashrif* (honoring), where divine favor is directly linked to how one treated the Qur'an during earthly life. The scene culminates with Allah’s oath to honor those who honored the Qur'an, emphasizing its central role in intercession and reward.
